newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA BEAT ITALY TO BOOK PLACE IN MEDAL ROUND.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA BEAT ITALY TO BOOK PLACE IN MEDAL ROUND.

text.p: Dean Evason had a goal and an assist to lead Canada to a 6-0 win over Italy and place in the medal round at the ice hockey world championship on Saturday.
"Our team was obviously determined to get to Helsinki and play for a medal," said Canadian coach Andy Murray. "Hopefully we're on an upward trend in terms of our play."
Needing at least a draw to advance, Canada went to work quickly, taking a 2-0 first period lead on goals by Jeff Friesen of the San Jose Sharks and Keith Primeau of the Hartford Whalers.

The Canadians continued their no-nonsense approach in the second as they physically overpowered the smaller Italians, increasing their advantage to 5-0 with goals from New York Islanders Travis Green and San Jose Sharks team-mates Owen Nolan and Bob Errey.
Evason, the only non-NHL player on the Canadian team, completed the scoring in the third.
A solid two-way effort was backed up by strong goaltending from Hartford Whalers Sean Burke and Tampa Bay Lightnings Rick Tabaracci in the Canadian net.
Burke, who has started all five games, was replaced by Tabaracci at the start of the third, the two men sharing in their second shutout of the tournament.
With the win Canada improved their record to 3-1-1 and join Sweden and the United States from the B pool in the medal round which begins on Monday in Helsinki.
"Canada had just a little too much of everything for us," said Italian coach Brian Lefley. "Playing against a team like Canada is difficult anytime.
"They're starting to show how they can play and starting to peak at the right time."
In A pool action, defending champions the Czech Republic, already assured a place in the medal round, closed out round-robin play by hammering France 9-3.
Martin Prochazka and David Vyborny paced the Czech attack with two goals each with singles going to Jiri Vykoukal, Robert Lang, Pavel Patera, Robert Reichel and Viktor Ujcik.
Robert Bozon, a former-member of the St. Louis Blues, scored twice for France.
